title: Pain relief after surgery (epidural catheter, pump)
what: After surgery, pain medicine is given continuously - through a thin tube in the back or through a pump into a vein. With a pump, you press the button yourself when it hurts.
why: After big surgery on the belly, chest or joints, when ordinary injections and pills are not enough.
duration: usually 1 to 3 days after surgery, then you switch to pills
tell_doctor: Blood-thinning medicines - your doctor will tell you what to stop and when
If strong painkillers have caused nausea or confusion before

prepare.title: Talk
prepare.text: The anesthesiologist will tell you in advance which pain relief method suits you.

prepare.title: Button
prepare.text: If you will have a pump, you will be shown how to press the button. Ask if anything is unclear.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor about everything you take.

bring: Glasses, if you need them - to see the button and the pump screen
steps: An epidural catheter is usually placed before surgery
You sit or lie on your side and your back is numbed with an injection
A thin tube is inserted in your back and taped with a plaster
The pump is connected to the catheter or to a vein
When it hurts, you press the button and the pump gives a dose of medicine
Nurses check your pain, blood pressure and breathing
feel: The pain is usually much less, but not always completely gone
Sometimes your legs go numb or weak, or you feel itching or nausea
You will not get too much: the pump will not give more than a safe dose
after: The catheter is taken out quickly and almost painlessly
Tell the nurse if the pain becomes strong again
red_flags: Severe drowsiness, hard to wake, slow breathing - call the nurse right away
Your legs do not move or your back hurts badly
Redness or discharge at the catheter site

faq.q: Can my family press the button for me?
faq.a: No. Only the patient presses the button - this keeps the pump safe.

faq.q: Will I get used to the painkiller?
faq.a: With short use after surgery this is rare. The doctor watches the dose.

reminders.text: Surgery tomorrow. If anything is unclear about pain relief afterward, ask the anesthesiologist.
